heroHeadline: SAC Bombs Kyauktaw Schools Killing 19 Students; Junta Launches Longest Tanintharyi Offensive Since Coup; 7 PDF-Zoland Fighters Killed in Chin Airstrike
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,922 of Myanmar's civil war (May 8, 2026), junta forces launched the longest military offensive in Tanintharyi Region since the 2021 coup, displacing over 6,000 civilians from 8 villages in Thayetchaung Township. A SAC airstrike on Phunom village in Tedim Township, Chin State, killed 7 PDF-Zoland fighters and 3 civilians — the day after the junta recaptured Kennedy Peak in Tedim. A separate airstrike on May 7 struck two private boarding schools in Kyauktaw, Rakhine State, killing 19 high school students and injuring over 20. KIA forces seized multiple junta camps in Bhamo and Waingmaw (Kachin State), tightening encirclement of Infantry Battalion 58 to within 100 meters. On the diplomatic front, former ASEAN foreign ministers and UN officials formally called for abandoning Myanmar's Five-Point Consensus and recognizing the NUG as the legitimate government, as the Philippine Senate urged ASEAN/UN court action against the junta.
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group, Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, Narinjara News, Global Arakan Network, Kachin Human Rights Watch, Aryan Age, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Committee to Protect Journalists, and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, and PDF statements.
